turns.assessment: The evidence indicates a brief optical polarization transient on the S15→S09 direction. Multiple channels and services received at S09 accumulated only two errored seconds, protected services switched for 1.2 s and restored, while power, OSNR, DGD, SOP-rate, amplifier, and pump measurements showed no sampled change. That is characteristic of a millisecond-scale SOP transient, but the observations cannot distinguish which of the four S15→S09 fibre spans caused it, so no repair location reaches the commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: A fast polarization event on S15→S09 span0 could affect all channels received at S09, cause the two errored seconds and short protection switches, and escape sampled optical telemetry.
Span1 is equally consistent with the common-channel transient and cannot be separated from the other spans by the available measurements.
Span2 is equally consistent with a brief all-channel polarization disturbance without sustained power, OSNR, or DGD change.
Span3 immediately preceding S09 could produce the observed receiver-side errors, but there is no evidence localizing the transient to this span rather than the other three.
A brief mechanical disturbance could cause a short power excursion missed by telemetry, though the complete absence of sampled power changes makes a pure SOP transient more likely.
